newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI sees record parent current profit for 96/97.
newsitem.headline: DDI sees record parent current profit for 96/97.

text.p: DDI Corp said on Tuesday that its parent current profit for the year ending on March 31 is likely to grow to record levels of over 60 billion yen.
DDI president Yusai Okuyama told Reuters in an interview that the company will announce its revised earnings forecast for the year later this week.
In November, DDI predicted that its parent current profit would be around 60 billion yen for 1996/97, up from its actual profit of 57.69 billion yen the previous year.

A planned cut in the access charges the company pays to Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) for use of NTT facilities was behind the planned upward revision in the firm's 1996/97 earnings estimate, the president said.
Okuyama said DDI, a leading operator of domestic long-distance telecom services, would pay a higher dividend than its earlier estimate of 1,380 yen per share for 1996/97.
He said DDI would keep a pledge to maintain its payout ratio -- the percentage of profits paid to shareholders in the form of dividends -- at 13 percent.
But Okuyama did not specify to what extent the company's dividend payment will be raised for 1996/97.

The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Sunday that NTT would cut its interconnection charges by 12 percent. The paper said the new rates would be retroactively applied to long-distance telecommunications companies from April 1996.
Asked about the report, Okuyama said a virtual pact has already been reached with NTT on a reduction in access charges.

The lower access charges should raise the company's profit in 1996/97, but about half of that increase may be offset by the effect of a recent cut in rates for long-distance services and various discounts that DDI has introduced, he said.
As a result, he said DDI's parent current profit would grow to a record level of above 60 billion yen in 1996/97. He declined to give any earnings estimate for 1997/98.

DDI forecast that its two mobile phone systems will continue growing. These are a cellular phone system and a Personal Handyphone System (PHS), a Japan-developed, cheaper version of the traditional cell phone technology.
Okuyama said DDI would have 10 million PHS and cellular phone subscribers by the end of March 1999, compared with the current level of about six million.
Despite the rapid increase in the number of subscribers, Okuyama said the PHS business was unlikely to become profitable earlier than the originally expected date of 1998/99.
"It will be hard to make the business profitable next fiscal year," he said.
DDI aims to start offering local call services as early as next fiscal year in areas close to major cities, where there should be good demand, he said.
